original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: What paid-local-mass reduction budget does the inherited packing relaxation imply for the selected complex word, as a function of the target saving? Exact answer: treating the removed mass as free and re-packing it as ideal rank-51 idle children, the whole-child curve is 0.001690054109089 (0 removed) -> 0.003081073334575 (all 2412 rank-1) -> 0.004028350731628 (+rank-2) -> 0.006916067471101 (+rank-3) -> 0.009650209177053 (+rank-4) -> 0.013070495581102 (+rank-5) -> 0.013675160009708 (all 5586 paid mass). Reaching the published bit primitive budget 0.00173343 needs removing at least 2.3948528% of paid mass (133.78 units per call); reaching the 1/99 planning target needs 92.7698485% (5182.12 units). The full-elimination ceiling is 8.0916x the inherited ceiling and only 1.354x the 1/99 target.
scope_change_reason: The card's acceptance gate asks for a new physically realizable contract whose per-call profile beats the selected word's packing ceiling. This session does not propose a contract; it builds the screening instrument the card's first experiment prescribes. The deliverable is the exact optimistic moment as a function of the one quantity any such contract must state, its per-call paid mass, plus the two decision thresholds. It therefore refines the card instead of answering its acceptance gate, and claims no supplier.
bottleneck_link: The complex side binds the selected kappa. This converts 'a proposal must lower the local excess spend' into an exact entrance fee: no change confined to this word's mass distribution can make the bit side bind unless it removes at least 2.3949% of paid local mass at zero realization cost, and no such change reaches the 1/99 planning target unless it removes 92.77% of it.
stop_rule: Stop at the exact ceiling of each whole-child breakpoint, the three decision thresholds, the optimality check of the lowest-rank-first removal rule and the nine controls. Do not attempt a physical realization, a new local word, a coverage-law change or a kappa claim.
evidence: Exact rational enclosures (256-bit) from the pinned predecessor module, run by verify.py; output PASS_COMPLEX_PAID_MASS_BUDGET. (1) phi=0 reproduces the predecessor's certified ceiling 0.001690054109089; (2) the seven whole-child breakpoints give strictly increasing certified ceilings ending at 0.013675160009708; (3) per-unit saving r^-a m^(a-1) - R^-a m^(a-1) is strictly positive and strictly decreasing in r at a = 1/1000, 1/500, 1/100, 1/20, and a rank-reversed removal of the same half-mass costs strictly more; (4) full elimination equals the closed-form pure-idle moment (7232/51)*(51/73)^(1-a) at three exponents; (5) phi thresholds 0.023948528 (a = 0.00173343), 0.148297888 (a = 0.002), 0.927698485 (a = 1/99) with bisection tolerance 1e-9 mass units; (6) a target 0.001 above the full-elimination ceiling is reported unreachable. Nine controls rejected. The card's first working example, python3 -B research/complex-local-word-ceiling/verify.py, prints PASS_COMPLEX_LOCAL_WORD_CEILING a_ceiling 0.00169005410908900006.

open_questions.question: Is the elimination axis attainable by any stated physical decoder or helper interface?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The budget curve is a favorable relaxation; a real interface pays for removing paid mass, so the physical entrance fee is strictly above these thresholds. Until one candidate states a per-call profile below 5586 paid mass units, the card's acceptance gate is untouched.
open_questions.first_step: Take one submitted candidate's per-call paid profile and run ceiling.ceiling() on it, then subtract the charged removal cost from the reported gain.
open_questions.blocked_by: No submitted candidate states a per-call paid profile below 5586 mass units under this coverage law.

open_questions.question: How does the elimination budget scale with the port count V?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The budget B(a) grows with w = 2*pairs*V/stages. If a wider word's paid mass grows more slowly than w, the required phi falls and wider words become a route to the 1/99 target without a coverage-law change.
open_questions.first_step: Run the same curve on a recorded complex word at a different V on a comparable template.
open_questions.blocked_by: Per-call paid profiles at other V are not collected in one place.

open_questions.question: Can the eight rank-8 centre children be eliminated more cheaply than the generic rank-51 re-packing assumes?
open_questions.why_it_matters: They are the last and per-unit most valuable group in the curve; a centre-sharing contract could remove them at a cost this relaxation does not model.
open_questions.first_step: Bind a submitted centre-sharing contract to its eliminated per-call centre mass and compare with the last two breakpoints.
open_questions.blocked_by: Centre-sharing proposals state sharing ratios rather than eliminated mass.
